'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Nuclear program of Iran]]
**[[Iran]] reports that a blackout at its underground [[Natanz]] nuclear facility is an act of [[nuclear terrorism]] and says that they reserve the right to respond, but it does not specify who was responsible or how they would respond. Parts of the [[electrical grid]] at Iran's main nuclear facilities at Natanz have been compromised. Intelligence sources claim in [[Israel]]i media that the [[Mossad]] intelligence agency carried out a [[cyber attack]] on the facility. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/4/11/incident-at-iranian-nuclear-site-targeted-by-blast-last-year (Al Jazeera)]
*[[War in Donbas (2014–2022)|War in Donbass]]
**A [[Ukrainian Ground Forces|Ukrainian soldier]] is killed and another is seriously wounded by [[Russian Separatist forces in Donbas|Russian separatist forces]] artillery fire on the [[front line]] in [[Eastern Ukraine]], bringing the total number of troops killed in combat this year to 27. [https://apnews.com/article/world-news-ukraine-antony-blinken-russia-e30cceb6a90d69dc087079282d3bce9c (AP)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*The [[Cambodia]]n Ministry of Culture and exiled politician [[Mu Sochua]] condemn American-Canadian [[digital media]] company ''[[Vice Media|Vice]]'' for publishing an article about an art project aiming to [[Hand-colouring of photographs|colorize]] photographs of inmates interred at [[Khmer Rouge]]-era prison [[Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum|Tuol Sleng]], after [[social media]] users noticed that the photos were edited to have the subjects smiling. The article was subsequently deleted. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/4/11/cambodia-condemns-vice-for-altered-khmer-rouge-images (Al Jazeera)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Sohag train collision]]
**[[Egypt]]'s prosecution service declares that nobody was at the controls of one of the trains that collided last month, in an accident that killed 20 people and injured around 200. [https://english.alaraby.co.uk/english/news/2021/4/11/egypt-train-crash-driver-was-not-at-the-controls (The New Arab)]
*[[Search and rescue|Rescue operations]] commence in [[Hutubi County|Hutubi]], [[Xinjiang]], [[China]], after a coal mine floods, trapping workers. Eight miners have been freed, but 21 still remain trapped. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-china-56706520 (BBC News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[India]] reports 152,879 new confirmed cases of COVID-19, a record for the sixth consecutive day. The country also reports 839 deaths in the past 24 hours, which is the highest daily total since October 18. [https://www.business-standard.com/article/current-affairs/india-s-covid-active-cases-breach-1-1-mn-mark-record-daily-high-of-152-879-121041100180_1.html (''Business Standard'')]
****The [[Ministry of Health and Family Welfare]] bans the export of the anti-viral drug [[Remdesivir]], and the ingredients used to make it, following an increase in the number of COVID-19 cases. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-india/india-bans-remdesivir-exports-as-coronavirus-rages-on-rallies-continue-idUSKBN2BY03T?il=0 (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Bangladesh]]
****[[Bangladesh]] reports 78 deaths from [[COVID-19]], a record for the second consecutive day, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 9,739. [https://www.dhakatribune.com/bangladesh/2021/04/11/daily-covid-19-deaths-in-bangladesh-reach-record-high-for-a-second-day (''Dhaka Tribune'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Iraq]]
****[[Iraq]] receives 50,000 doses of the [[Pfizer–BioNTech vaccine]]. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/latest-on-coronavirus-outbreak/iraq-gets-first-batch-of-pfizer-biontech-vaccine/2205247 (Anadolu Agency)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Pakistan]]
****[[Pakistan]] reports 114 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, which is the highest number of deaths this year, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 15,443. [https://www.geo.tv/latest/344666-pakistan-records-highest-number-of-deaths-for-2021-in-a-single-day-from-coronavirus (Geo News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]]
****The [[Greater Manila Area]], the provinces of [[Abra (province)|Abra]] and [[Quirino]], and the city of [[Santiago, Isabela]], are placed under the looser [[COVID-19 community quarantines in the Philippines|modified enhanced community quarantine]] until the end of April. [https://www.rappler.com/nation/ncr-plus-mecq-philippines-quarantines-april-2021 (Rappler)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]]
****[[Thailand]] reports a record 967 new confirmed cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of cases to 32,625. [https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/2098343/record-high-967-new-covid-cases-sunday (''Bangkok Post'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***[[COVID-19 vaccination in Australia]]
****[[Prime Minister of Australia|Prime Minister]] [[Scott Morrison]] abandons the country's plan to [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccinate]] all [[Australian people|Australian]]s by the end of the year amidst medical advice that makes the vaccination program uncertain. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-04-11/scott-morrison-abandons-covid-19-vaccination-target/100061998 (ABC Australia)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in California]]
****[[California]] surpasses 60,000 deaths from COVID-19. [https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2021-04-11/californias-covid-19-death-toll-surpasses-60-000 (''The Los Angeles Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Cameroon]]
***[[Cameroon]] receives 200,000 doses of the [[Sinovac]] [[BBIBP-CorV]] [[vaccine]] from [[China]], which will be used in the first phase of their vaccination campaign. [https://www.barrons.com/articles/china-gives-200-000-covid-19-vaccine-doses-to-cameroon-01618175105 (''Barron's'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
***[[Minister of Health (France)|Health Minister]] [[Olivier Véran]] confirms that all people aged 55 and over would be eligible for a vaccine starting tomorrow, which is a week earlier than originally scheduled, with [[Oxford-AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|AstraZeneca]], and a single-dose [[Johnson & Johnson COVID-19 vaccine|Johnson & Johnson]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]s. [https://www.connexionfrance.com/French-news/Covid-vaccines-jabs-vaccinations-open-for-over-55s-in-France-says-health-minister (The Connexion)]
**[[COVID-19 vaccine]], [[501.V2 variant]]
***An Israeli study finds that the [[Pfizer–BioNTech vaccine]] may be less effective against the [[South Africa]]n variant when compared to other strains of the virus. [https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/world/south-african-variant-may-evade-protection-from-pfizer-vaccine-israeli-study-says/ar-BB1fxbW5?ocid=uxbndlbing (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Killing of Daunte Wright]], [[Daunte Wright protests]]
**A police officer in [[Brooklyn Center, Minnesota]], a suburb of [[Minneapolis]], kills a man during an attempted arrest following a [[traffic stop]], leading to [[protests]] and [[riots]] in the city and surrounding areas. [https://www.startribune.com/brooklyn-center-police-fatally-shoot-man-20-inflaming-tensions-during-the-derek-chauvin-trial/600044821/ (''Minneapolis Star-Tribune'')]
*An [[Egypt]]ian court [[sentence (law)|sentences]] university student Ahmed Bassam Zaki to an additional eight years in prison for [[sexually assault]]ing and [[blackmail]]ing at least three women between 2016 and 2020. The case led to a public debate about [[sexual harassment]] and abuse within the country. Zaki was previously sentenced to three years in prison by a different court in December. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-egypt-harassment/egyptian-court-jails-student-in-case-that-led-to-sex-crimes-debate-idUSKBN2BY0KT?il=0 (Reuters)]
*Seven [[Catholic Church in Haiti|Catholic]] [[Clergy#Catholicism|clergy]], including two French citizens, are kidnapped in [[Croix-des-Bouquets]], [[Ouest (department)|Ouest]], [[Haiti]]. [https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1417759/seven-catholic-clergy-including-two-french-kidnapped-in-haiti-church-spokesman (''Philippine Daily Inquirer'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Peruvian general election]], [[2017–2021 Peruvian political crisis]]
**Peruvians head to the polls to elect their president after having four presidents in four years. [https://www.cnn.com/2021/04/09/americas/peru-elections-fragmentation-scli-intl/index.html (CNN)]
*[[2021 Chadian presidential election]]
**Chadians head to the polls to elect their president. Incumbent [[Idriss Déby]] is expected to extend his three-decade mandate. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-chad-election/voting-starts-in-chad-presidential-election-idUSKBN2BY06Q?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[2021 Beninese presidential election]]
**After violent days of protests, [[Benin]]ese citizens head to the polls to elect their president. Incumbent [[Patrice Talon]] is expected to win his second term as most of his rivals are either in prison or in exile. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/4/11/benin-votes-in-presidential-election-opposition-sidelined (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2021 Ecuadorian general election]]
**Centre-right candidate [[Guillermo Lasso]] defeats [[socialist]] [[Andrés Arauz]] in the second round of voting in [[Ecuador]] for the [[President of Ecuador|presidency]]. [https://www.wsj.com/articles/ecuadors-guillermo-lasso-wins-presidential-election-11618195085 (''The Wall Street Journal'')]
*[[2021 Kyrgyz constitutional referendum]]
**Kyrgyz citizens head to the polls on a [[referendum]] to reform the Constitution. If approved, it would increase the powers of incumbent [[populist]] President [[Sadyr Zhaparov]] and allow him to run for a second term. It would also reduce the size of the parliament by 25%. [https://www.dw.com/en/kyrgyzstan-holds-vote-on-whether-to-strengthen-presidency/a-57160057 (DW)]
*[[2021 German federal election]]
**[[Bavaria]]n [[Minister president (Germany)|minister president]] [[Markus Söder]] and [[Leader of the Christian Democratic Union|leader]] of the ruling [[Christian Democratic Union of Germany|Christian Democratic Union]] [[Armin Laschet]] announce their respective candidacies to succeed current [[Chancellor of Germany|Chancellor]] [[Angela Merkel]] after the federal elections take place. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-04-11/germany-s-soeder-said-to-signal-bid-for-chancellor-after-merkel (Bloomberg)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2021 Masters Tournament]]
**[[Hideki Matsuyama]] wins the [[2021 Masters Tournament|85th edition]] of the [[Masters Tournament|Masters]] to become first male Japanese major champion. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-golf-masters/golf-japans-matsuyama-hangs-on-to-make-history-with-masters-win-idUSKBN2BY0KV (Reuters)]
*[[WrestleMania 37]]
**The first [[WWE]] show with fans in attendance since March 2020 takes place in [[Tampa, Florida|Tampa]], [[Florida]], US. [https://www.cbssports.com/wwe/news/2021-wwe-wrestlemania-37-results-recap-grades-sasha-banks-bianca-belair-steal-show-in-historic-main-event/live/ (CBS Sports)]
